full_parsed_JSON.title: Singhi's conjecture on prime projective planes
full_parsed_JSON.statement: A projective plane $\sigma$ is a **subplane** of a projective plane $\pi$ if $\sigma$ is a subsystem of $\pi$. A projective plane is **prime** if it has no proper projective subplane. Let $\mathcal{F}$ denote the free projective plane, and let projective planes over prime fields mean those over $\mathbb{Q}$ or over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for a prime $p$. **Singhi's conjecture.** The projective planes over prime fields and the free projective plane $\mathcal{F}$ are the only prime projective planes. Every prime projective plane is a homomorphic image of $\mathcal{F}$, which motivates the conjecture; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
full_parsed_JSON.source_name: Bhaskar Bagchi, “A coding theoretic approach to the uniqueness conjecture for projective planes of prime order”, arXiv:1801.07038 (2018).

full_parsed_JSON.title: Condition (I) conjecture for the elementary divisors of quasihomogeneous singularities
full_parsed_JSON.statement: Let $f\in\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a quasihomogeneous singularity. full_parsed_JSON.title: Proudfoot–Xu–Young negative-root conjecture for matroid Z-polynomials
full_parsed_JSON.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid with lattice of flats $L(M)$, and let $M_F$ and $M^F$ denote the corresponding localization and restriction notation used in the source. Its $Z$-polynomial is

$$
Z_M(t):=\sum_{F\in L(M)}t^{\operatorname{rk} M_F}P_{M^F}(t).
$$

**Proudfoot–Xu–Young's conjecture.** The polynomial $Z_M(t)$ has only negative zeros for every matroid $M$. The source gives no resolution of this conjecture for arbitrary matroids.

full_parsed_JSON.title: The sharp snowflake exponent conjecture for modulus metrics on networks
full_parsed_JSON.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected network, let $d_p$ denote its modulus metric for $p\in[1,\infty]$, and let $s(p)$ be the supremum of the exponents $t$ such that $d_p^t$ is a metric on every connected network. For the path graph $P_3$ on three nodes, the preceding calculation gives the upper bound $s(p)\leq p/(p-1)$ for $1<p<\infty$, with the endpoint values $s(1)=\infty$ and $s(\infty)=1$. **Sharp snowflake exponent conjecture.** For all $p\in[1,\infty]$, 

$$
s(p)=\frac{p}{p-1}.
$$

Namely, $P_3$ demonstrates the worst-case behavior. The conjecture asserts that the path graph gives the sharp obstruction to the triangle inequality for powers of modulus metrics. It has been answered in the affirmative using the theory of Fulkerson duality for modulus.

full_parsed_JSON.title: Difference-product and difference-quotient sum-product conjectures
full_parsed_JSON.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ be finite, and define

$$
A-A=\{a-b:a,b\in A\},\qquad AA^{-1}=\{ab^{-1}:a,b\in A\},
$$

with the convention $0^{-1}=0$. Also let $AA=\{ab:a,b\in A\}$. **Difference-product and difference-quotient conjecture.** For every fixed $\delta\leq 1$, one has both

$$
|A-A|+|AA^{-1}|\gtrsim |A|^{1+\delta},
$$

and

$$
|A-A|+|AA|\gtrsim |A|^{1+\delta}.
$$

These are sum-product-type expansion claims involving differences together with quotients or products. The candidate is presented without a name or resolution evidence, so its status remains open.

full_parsed_JSON.title: The prime-divisor positivity implication for Goldbach convolution sums
full_parsed_JSON.statement:
Let $N$ be an integer, let $p$ range over the primes dividing $N$, and let $\Lambda_0$ denote the function used in the source. **Prime-divisor positivity conjecture.** If

$$
\sum_{p\mid N}\sum_{n\leq \frac{N}{p}}\Lambda_0(n)\Lambda_0(N/p-n)>0,
$$

then

$$
\sum_{n\leq \frac{N}{p}}\Lambda_0(n)\Lambda_0(N/p-n)>0
$$

for every prime $p$ dividing $N$. The text proposes this implication as the statement through which the Goldbach conjecture will be attacked, but supplies no resolution.

full_parsed_JSON.title: Cloys and Fox's conjecture on neighborhood-prime lobsters
full_parsed_JSON.statement:
A **lobster** is a tree in which deleting all leaves leaves a caterpillar. A graph is neighborhood-prime if it admits a bijective labeling by consecutive positive integers such that the greatest common divisor of the labels in every nontrivial vertex neighborhood is $1$.

**Cloys and Fox's lobster conjecture.** Every lobster is neighborhood-prime.

The source proves the claim for several classes of lobsters, including reduced lobsters under specified degree restrictions, and explains that a proof for all caterpillars being prime would imply the lobster claim. The conjecture remains unresolved in the source.

\nabla_p=\sup_{v\in V}\sum_{x,y\in V}\tau_p(v,x)\tau_p(x,y)\tau_p(y,v).
$$

The **triangle condition** is the condition $\nabla_{p_c}<\infty$.

**Triangle condition conjecture.** One has $\nabla_{p_c}<\infty$.

The triangle condition is a sufficient condition for mean-field critical behaviour and is known in several settings, including high-dimensional Euclidean lattices. Whether it holds for every nonamenable quasi-transitive graph remains open.

full_parsed_JSON.title: Finiteness conjecture for Type (i) and Type (iia) power mappings
full_parsed_JSON.statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a prime with $p>2n$, and partition the reduced residues modulo $p$ into residue classes $I_i$ modulo $n$. Let $f(x)=Ax^k\pmod p$ be a power permutation. Type (i) means that $f(I_i)=I_i$ for every $i$, while Type (iia) means that $f(I_i)=I_{\sigma(i)}$ for some permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$. **Finiteness conjecture.** Excluding $f(x)=x\pmod p$, there are only finitely many Type (i) examples. Excluding $f(x)=\pm x\pmod p$, there are only finitely many Type (iia) examples. The conjecture formalizes the observed sparsity of these mappings beyond the trivial examples; the supplied text does not state a resolution.

full_parsed_JSON.title: The universal deviation inequality for good drawings of complete graphs
full_parsed_JSON.statement:
Let $D$ be a good drawing of the complete graph $K_n$, let $\mathcal{F}(D)$ denote its set of faces, and fix a face $F\in\mathcal{F}(D)$. Let $\hat{\Delta}_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor-2}(D)$ and $\bar{\Delta}_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor-2}(D)$ denote the corresponding deviation quantities defined for $D$ with respect to $F$.

**Universal deviation inequality.** For every face $F\in\mathcal{F}(D)$,

$$
\hat{\Delta}_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor-2}(D)\geq \bar{\Delta}_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor-2}(D).
$$

The paper reports that this condition held for all drawings and faces inspected and proposes it for all good drawings of complete graphs. Its general validity is left open.

full_parsed_JSON.title: Nakamura's strong c-Wilf equivalence conjecture
full_parsed_JSON.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{S}_m$ denote the symmetric group on $m$ letters, and let $\pi,\tau\in\mathfrak{S}_m$. Write $\pi\sim\tau$ for ordinary Wilf-equivalence and $\pi\overset{s}{\sim}\tau$ for strong c-Wilf equivalence. **Nakamura's conjecture.** For all $\pi,\tau\in\mathfrak{S}_m$,

$$
\pi\sim\tau\quad\text{if and only if}\quad \pi\overset{s}{\sim}\tau.
$$

This conjecture asks whether ordinary Wilf-equivalence and strong c-Wilf equivalence coincide. The source notes that the analogous statement for ordinary Wilf-equivalence is already false for patterns of length $3$, and says that this conjecture appears to evade the methods developed in the paper.

full_parsed_JSON.title: DeMarco–Kahn upper tail conjecture for strictly balanced graphs and dense regimes
full_parsed_JSON.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph, let $m_H$ denote its appearance-threshold parameter, and let the DeMarco–Kahn upper tail conjecture be the assertion that the upper-tail estimate stated above holds. A graph is **strictly balanced** when the relevant density parameter is strictly maximized by $H$ rather than by a proper subgraph. **DeMarco–Kahn's restricted upper tail conjecture.** The DeMarco–Kahn upper tail conjecture is true for every strictly balanced graph $H$. Moreover, for every fixed $\gamma>0$, it is true under the additional assumption

$$
p\geqslant n^{-1/m_H+\gamma}.
$$

These are proposed restricted regimes in which the false general conjecture may still hold. The paper presents them as open problems rather than proving them.
full_parsed_JSON.source_name: Matas Šileikis and Lutz Warnke, “A counterexample to the DeMarco-Kahn Upper Tail Conjecture”, arXiv:1809.09595 (2019).
full_parsed_JSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.09595

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2018). “We leave it as an intriguing open problem to formulate an upper tail conjecture for graphs which are not strictly balanced (this would already be interesting for balanced graphs).”

full_parsed_JSON.title: Bounded odd Gaussian-prime representation conjecture
full_parsed_JSON.statement:
Let $\Gamma_G$ denote the Gaussian integers under consideration in the source, and let

$$
K_\pi=\{z\in\pi_{\mathbb{Z}[i]}\mid\operatorname{Re}(z)\geq0\text{ and }\operatorname{Im}(z)\geq0\}.
$$

**Bounded odd Gaussian-prime representation conjecture.** There are constants $c_0$ and $k_0$ such that, for every $z\in\Gamma_G$ with $\max(\operatorname{Re}(z),\operatorname{Im}(z))\geq c_0$, $z$ is a sum of at most $k_0$ odd primes from $K_\pi$. This is formulated using the preceding theorem and an integer additive hypothesis; it remains open in the source.
full_parsed_JSON.source_name: Felix Sidokhine, “Shnirelman's Theorem Applications”, arXiv:2001.00063 (2019).
